national_sources.name: the Statistical Office of the Slovak Republic

notes.inflation: Inflation is the EU's harmonised index (HICP), the measure the ECB targets, which can differ by a few tenths from the Statistical Office's national CPI. Slovakia joined the euro on 1 January 2009 and has had no policy rate of its own since: the rate shown is the European Central Bank's deposit facility rate, from that date.
notes.labour: Unemployment is Eurostat's monthly, seasonally adjusted rate (ILO definition, ages 15 to 74). Slovak news often quotes the labour office's registered unemployment rate instead, a different measure. Employment and participation rates are the OECD's quarterly figures for ages 15 to 64.
notes.trade: Goods trade is Eurostat's monthly total with the rest of the world, in euros. Cars and electronics dominate Slovakia's exports, so the balance moves with the car industry and with energy import prices.
notes.public: Debt and the budget balance are Eurostat's excessive deficit procedure figures for general government, calendar years, so the latest year is a year ahead of the IMF's.
notes.markets: The 10-year yield is the OECD's monthly average of the Slovak government yield, which runs about a month behind; the exchange rates are the Federal Reserve's daily euro rates, shared with every euro area page.
